claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.

In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it starts, while an execution that is already running in the stage is protected.

In a CodePipeline pipeline using the default `SUPERSEDED` mode whose CodeBuild stage runs `pulumi up`, if enough commits land while the stage is busy, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue so each one runs in turn rather than a later commit superseding an earlier waiting one.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType` V2).
To use `QUEUED` execution mode, both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set when defining the pipeline.
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can be used to set the pipeline's `executionMode` and `pipelineType`.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The link target /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ exists as the API docs page for the `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource is described in the section below this one ('Manage the pipeline with Pulumi') in the same page.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack concurrently, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that prevents concurrent runs of a deployment job targeting that environment.
An exclusive lock check is added to an Azure DevOps environment from that environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
Azure Pipelines stages support a `lockBehavior` property that is set on the stage referencing the environment with the exclusive lock check.
The default value of the Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` stage property is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run is run against the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, running them one at a time in order.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The docs page exists at /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ for the `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource.
A documentation page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ describing Pulumi update conflicts.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts `command`, `stack`, and `args` inputs, with `command: up` and `args: --yes` running a non-interactive update.
When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent runs reach the same stack, the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict error.

TeamCity's default behavior is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available, so nothing prevents concurrent builds from racing on the same Pulumi stack by default.
The link target /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ (update conflicts troubleshooting page) exists.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds', located under the configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to `0`, meaning unlimited.

Setting the TeamCity 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option to `1` causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and run only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior for a stack.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment that a deployment job targets serializes deployments, so Pulumi updates to the same stack do not run concurrently.
Azure Pipelines supports a `lockBehavior: sequential` setting on a stage, used together with an exclusive lock check on the environment.

The Pulumi docs page for Azure DevOps (/docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/) has a section titled 'Serialize deployments with an exclusive lock' (anchor #serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock).
AWS CodePipeline has a pipeline execution mode setting that can be set to `QUEUED`, so that waiting executions run in turn.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer pipeline execution supersede an older execution that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page for AWS code services (/docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/) has a section titled 'Serialize pipeline executions' (anchor #serialize-pipeline-executions).
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds', and setting it to 1 prevents concurrent runs of the deployment build.
The Pulumi docs page for TeamCity (/docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/) has a section titled 'Limit concurrent builds' (anchor #limit-concurrent-builds).
